about: Names, descriptions and grades are the official PlayStation 5 list, shown as published. Kinds, roadmap stages, missable flags and progress targets are this guide's own work, built from the official descriptions and the counts PlayStation tracks. Every guide below is written for this app, in our own words; the sources each one rests on are named beside it.

list.label: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5): the official list, names, descriptions and grades

own.label: Guide text: our own advice, written from the official description for this app

targets.label: PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies: PSN's progress targets and counts

trophies.guide: The platinum, awarded on its own once the other 54 trophies are all earned — there is nothing separate to do for it. Work the roadmap in this app from stage 1 to stage 7 and it unlocks the moment the last of the 54 lands; if it does not pop, the usual cause is one trophy still short of its count, so check the counters here against the targets first.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Story trophy for the opening mission, Gone Fishing. It is the first thing the game asks of you, so it cannot be missed or done out of order: play through the prologue and the trophy lands as the mission wraps up. Nothing to prepare — just start the story.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Chapter 1, the first full chapter after the opening mission. Follow the story markers and complete every mission the chapter gives you; the trophy pops at the chapter's end. No choices or side content are needed, and it cannot be missed while playing the story.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Chapter 2 (the name is censored exactly as PlayStation publishes it). Keep following the main story after Chapter 1 and the trophy lands when the chapter closes. Before pushing deep into a new chapter, glance at the Missables page: the one-time moments flagged there sit inside story missions like these.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Chapter 3. Play the main missions in order and it unlocks as the chapter ends. By now the map and activity list are opening up, but nothing in this chapter needs a detour — the collectible and activity sweeps in the roadmap are all still waiting for you afterwards.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Chapter 4, the last numbered chapter before the endgame. Complete its missions in order and the trophy pops at the chapter break. Keep a manual save before the final stretch of the story: the flagged missable moments are all behind you by then only if you caught them on the way through.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: The gold story trophy, for completing the final mission of the game. It arrives at the end of the main storyline, after Chapter 4. Finishing the story does not lock you out of the state of Leonida — the stranger strands, collectibles and the 100% push in the later roadmap stages are all still there to clean up afterwards.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Story trophy for the named mission Breakfast Run. Named-mission trophies like this one are simply chapters of the main story: reach the mission, play it to its end, and the trophy is yours. If you are following the roadmap, it falls inside stage 1 in story order.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Story trophy for The Cartel Heist, a named set-piece mission in the main storyline. Play the story until the heist is offered, complete it, and the trophy pops. Heist-style missions are also where the game teaches the robbery systems the free-roam crime trophies in stage 5 build on, so it is worth learning them here.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Story trophy for the named mission Child's Play. Reach it in the main story and finish it. Like the other named-mission trophies it is unmissable while you are playing through the plot, and it sits in stage 1 of the roadmap in story order.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Story trophy for the named mission Headliners. Play the main story to this mission and complete it. Nothing in the official description suggests a choice or a one-time condition, so treat it as a straight story beat inside stage 1.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Story trophy for VCIA Takedown, the mission set around Vice City International Airport. Finish the mission for the trophy — and pay attention while you are at the airport: the missable trophy Catch Me If You Can (an unscheduled departure at VCIA) is tied to this same location and is flagged on the Missables page, so do not rush past the airport sequence.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Story trophy for the named mission Operation Savage Glory, one of the late main-story missions. Reach it, complete it, and the trophy lands. It is the last of the named-mission trophies in the list before the final mission's gold.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: The gold for reaching 100% completion on the game's own completion counter — the long tail of the platinum. GTA completion is never 'do literally everything': it is a defined checklist of story, strands, activities, collectibles and feats, and the counters in this app track the trophy-sized pieces of it (250 stunts, 100 WAiNK spots, 52 areas and the rest). Save it for last, work stages 2 to 6 first, and use the in-game completion screen to find what is still outstanding.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Complete 250 of the game's stunt challenges — the marked jumps and stunt spots scattered across Leonida. PSN tracks the count to 250, and the counter in this app does the same. Stunts are repeatable and never missable, so the efficient play is to clear them region by region alongside the exploration trophy (The Goodtime State, 52 areas) rather than in one grind at the end.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the game's 9 activity types once — the official count PlayStation tracks. You do not need to win or finish well, just start each type once: races, the shooting range, drone races, fishing, arcade games, bowling, meditation and the rest as they unlock. It falls out naturally if you sample every new icon the map offers during the story, and it is the cheapest trophy on the list.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold-medal all 42 Shooting Range challenges — every weapon course, at the gold score, not just a pass. PSN tracks the 42, and the counter here mirrors it. Ranges can be retried freely, so learn each course's target pattern at bronze pace first, then push for gold once your aim settings feel right; this is a skill trophy, not a missable one.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every one of the 14 locations — a win at each, not just an entry. The locations unlock as you explore, and each race can be retried until you win it, so nothing here is missable. Learn the drone's cornering on the first two courses and the rest is repetition; tick each location off in the counter as you clear it.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — the word 'different' is the catch: winning the same race 20 times does not count. Work through the race series across Leonida, one win per event, and let the counter here track how many distinct wins you have banked. Races stay available in free roam, so this is a stage 3 sweep, never a missable.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal — the fishing character — in one of his fishing challenges. Find Cal's challenge where fishing is offered, learn the casting and reeling rhythm on a practice fish first, then take the challenge and out-catch him. It can be retried, so a lost challenge costs you nothing but time.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game, start to finish, at any arcade cabinet you find in Leonida. 'Complete' means finishing the game, not just playing a credit, so pick the shortest cabinet you can find and see it through. One completion is all it takes.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's mission strand — every mission Andy gives you, through to his final one. Character strands like this run beside the main story and are picked up from the stranger and contact markers on the map. The trophy only lands on the strand's last mission, so if you have started Andy's jobs, see them through; strands stay available after the story, in stage 2 of the roadmap.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's mission strand, through to his final mission. Work each of Kenton's jobs as they appear on the map; the trophy pops when the strand closes, not before. Like the other character finales it belongs to stage 2, the side-story sweep after (or alongside) the main plot.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's mission strand through to his final mission. Pick up Billy's jobs from his map markers and keep returning until the strand ends — the trophy is for the last mission only. Character strands can be finished after the main story, so nothing here is lost by playing the plot first.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full mission strands for strangers, anywhere in Leonida — a strand means a stranger's whole chain of missions, not a single job. The named character finales in this list (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are strands of exactly this kind, so finishing those five leaves only three more strands to find. PSN tracks the 8; use the counter here to keep count as strands close.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's mission strand through to his final mission. Follow Randy's markers as the strand unfolds and complete each job; the trophy lands at the strand's end. It is one of the five named strands that feed the Strangers & Freaks silver, so it does double duty in stage 2.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's mission strand through to his final mission. Work Tyrone's jobs in order until the strand closes and the trophy pops. As with the other character finales, the strand waits for you after the story — stage 2 of the roadmap is built around clearing all five.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot in Leonida — 18 of them, the count PlayStation tracks. The spots sit at viewpoints and quiet places across the state, so the practical route is to meditate whenever a session leaves you near one and let the counter here keep the tally. None of the spots disappear, so this is a sweep, not a missable.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Take Bret's hunting job and bring down the unique animal he sends you after — a specific, named hunt, not any animal of the species. Start the job from Bret, follow its tracking steps to the animal, and finish the hunt. Because it is a set mission for a named character, it sits with the stage 2 strands.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Complete 3 full Collectible Card sets — every card in each of three sets, found out in the world. Cards are hidden pickups across Leonida, so this is a map sweep: work region by region, and note that you need three completed sets, not three cards. PSN tracks the sets finished; partial sets do not count, so finish the sets you start.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK It spot at 100 different locations across Leonida — the silver with the biggest scavenger hunt on the list. The spots are fixed world locations, and the count is tracked to 100, so treat it like the card sweep: clear a district at a time and keep the counter here honest. Pair it with The Goodtime State (all 52 areas) — the two sweeps cover the same ground.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 of the game's Challenges — the short scored tasks the world and its activities throw up. Challenges are plentiful and repeatable in kind, so this is a volume trophy: take challenges as they appear during the activity sweep rather than hunting them at the end, and let the counter track you to 50.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, earn a 4-star wanted level, then lose it and fully escape — the trophy needs the whole arc: the heat at 4 stars, your partner present, and a clean getaway. Deliberately raise the level somewhere with an escape route (alleys, water, a fast car), then break line of sight and stay hidden until the stars clear. It is a free-roam feat you can set up any time, in stage 5.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops in a row with your partner, keeping a wanted level alive the whole time — if the stars fully clear between shops, the chain breaks. Pick three shops close together, rob the first, and drive straight to the next while the heat is still on you; your partner must be with you for all three. Plan the route before the first robbery, not during it.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — a vehicle counts as discovered the first time you get in and drive it. Traffic variety rises in richer districts and around the airport and docks, so steal widely as you travel rather than farming one street. Most of the 100 arrives on its own during the other sweeps; the counter here shows what is left.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies inside one single use of Combat Focus, the game's slow-motion aiming state. Set it up where enemies cluster — a gang operation or a story shootout — line up your targets before you trigger it, and use a weapon that drops a target in one or two hits. If a run ends at four, nothing is lost: the setup can be repeated anywhere enemies gather.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an 'unscheduled departure' at VCIA — Vice City International Airport: in plain terms, get airborne out of the airport in a way the airport did not schedule, during the story's airport business. This is the list's clearest missable (see the Missables page): the chance is tied to the VCIA Takedown mission, so when the story takes you to VCIA, take a plane and leave instead of following the script out. Keep a manual save before that mission so a missed chance is recoverable.
trophies.missableNote: Flagged missable from the official description: the departure is at VCIA, the airport the story visits for VCIA Takedown — a scripted story location, not a free-roam one. Attempt it during that mission window; if you finish the story without it, a chapter replay is not confirmed, so keep a save before the airport mission.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: The description is a joke with the details hidden — 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos' — and a Rhino is the series' tank. The working reading: survive or win the story's tank encounter, the set-piece where the heat inside a Rhino is the point. We flag it missable (Missables page) because scripted vehicle set-pieces do not usually repeat in free roam: when a Rhino shows up in a mission, engage with it rather than running, and keep a save beforehand.
trophies.missableNote: Flagged missable from the official description: Rhinos are the game's tanks, and a tank encounter 'getting hot' reads as a scripted story set-piece rather than a free-roam event. When the story puts you in or against a Rhino, finish the encounter instead of fleeing it, and keep a save before big late-story missions.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store and get out without ever being detected — no alarm, no witness completing a call, no wanted level. Scout the store first: where the staff and cameras are, and which exit is quietest. Go in masked and unhurried, take what is in reach, and leave before anyone reacts; if a robbery goes loud, let it go and set up a fresh attempt at another store.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape each time — a robbery only counts once you are clear, not when the vault opens. Bank vaults are the heavy end of the crime list, so arrive with a fast car parked for the exit and an escape route in mind. The five can be done across free roam at your own pace; the counter here tracks the escapes, which are what count.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob one armored truck and escape with the take. Armored trucks run routes in free roam: stop the truck, deal with its guards, breach the rear doors, grab the cash and lose the heat that follows. One clean truck is enough — pick your moment on a quiet stretch of road rather than downtown.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — every one of its 52 areas, the count PlayStation tracks. An area counts once you have actually been into it, so this is a map-completion sweep: work the state district by district, including the water and the islands, and pair the route with the WAiNK spots and card sets, which hide in the same corners. The counter here turns a vague 'explore everything' into 52 boxes to fill.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of Leonida's 9 gangs — one operation per gang, all nine gangs covered. Operations sit in gang territory, so learn whose ground you are on before you go in; robbing the same gang twice does not advance the count. The counter here is best kept by gang, not by robbery.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach, the beach strip where the game opens. The name — 'In The Beginning…' — is the tell: this is an opening-hours moment, so we flag it missable (Missables page). Early on, when Ocean Beach is in front of you, find the bar or vendor serving cocktails, buy one and take in the view; do not leave it for the endgame clean-up on the assumption it will still be there.
trophies.missableNote: Flagged missable from the official description: the name ('In the beginning') ties the moment to the game's opening stretch, on Ocean Beach where the story starts. Have the cocktail early, while the opening is still in front of you, rather than assuming the moment waits all game.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in a car, through the glass, 'in classic style' — a nod to the series' oldest showroom exit. The description reads as a staged story set-piece rather than something free roam offers on demand, so it is flagged on the Missables page: when a mission leaves you inside a showroom with cars around you, drive out through the window instead of walking to the door.
trophies.missableNote: Flagged missable from the official description: smashing out of a showroom 'in classic style' is a set-piece exit, the kind a story mission stages once. If a mission puts you inside a vehicle showroom, leave through the glass in a car rather than on foot, and keep a save before missions set in dealerships.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Bowl at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley and complete the follow-through the description asks for — play a game at that specific alley, not any lane in Leonida. The alley is a named location, so head there once bowling is on your map, play your frames, and the trophy lands with the game. It also counts toward Master of None's activity types, so it does double duty in stage 3.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: A hidden trophy with a deliberately vague description — 'A partnership with mass appeal' — and no count to chase. The honest reading is that it is tied to the two protagonists' partnership and something the pair does together that draws a crowd or an audience. We do not flag it missable, because the description names no one-time place or mission; play the partner activities and story beats as they come, and if a moment with your partner turns into a public spectacle, you are probably looking at it. Where a description pins nothing down, this guide says so rather than inventing a location.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: A hidden trophy whose description is just 'Choices made (for better or worse)' — but PlayStation tracks a progress count for it, and the target is 500. So this is a volume trophy in disguise: make choices wherever the game offers them — dialogue, deals, deals gone wrong — and they add up. Five hundred is a lot, so start early, choose actively instead of letting prompts time out, and let the counter here show the climb.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: Another deliberately vague hidden description: 'Second time's the charm' — succeed at something on your second attempt, having failed it once. That shape is exactly why it is flagged on the Missables page: if the attempt belongs to a one-time event, never failing means never earning it. When the story hands you a challenge that can be failed and retried, failing once on purpose before you succeed is the safe route, and a manual save beforehand costs nothing.
trophies.missableNote: Flagged missable from the official description: 'Second time's the charm' means succeeding at something you first failed — and if the something is a one-time story event, a clean first-try success could lock the trophy out. Where a mission offers a retry-able challenge, a deliberate first failure is the safe play; keep a save before one-time events.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: A hidden trophy for witnessing something strange — 'What the hell just happened?' is the whole description. Leonida keeps its oddities out in the wilds and off the main roads, so the practical advice is to explore at night, follow up odd lights, sounds and strangers rather than driving past, and linger when something feels staged. It names no place and no count, so this guide will not invent one: it is an exploration trophy, and the stage 4 and 5 sweeps put you in the right places to trip over it.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock a person down with a melee drive-by — strike someone with a melee weapon from a moving vehicle as you pass them. Ride or drive slowly past a pedestrian on a pavement edge, swing as you pass, and make sure the hit lands from the vehicle, not after you stop and get out. It takes a few passes to learn the timing; a quiet street and a slow bike make it much easier.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering marked bills through your contacts — the take from robberies marked as hot money has to pass through the laundering route, and only what comes out clean counts. Feed every marked bill you lift into your contacts' laundering instead of spending around it, and the total climbs with your stage 5 crime sweep. PSN tracks the dollars; the counter here does the same.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops, in total — clothes, weapons, vehicles, services, everything the game's shops sell. It is a money sink that the rest of the list fills for you: by the time the garages and the crime sweep are done, most of the $100,000 has gone through a till. If you are short at the end, the fastest honest route is big-ticket vehicle and property spending you wanted anyway.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Buy every garage property in Leonida — all 8 of them, the count PlayStation tracks. Garages come up for sale as you explore and as your money grows, so this belongs late in the run (stage 6), once the heists and laundering have filled your account. Buy each garage as it lists rather than saving for a single spree; the counter here tracks the eight.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — take a vehicle, register it through the app, repeat ten times. It pairs naturally with Whip It Good (discover 100 vehicles): while you are stealing widely for that count, register the keepers as you go and both counters climb together. Ten registrations is an evening's habit, not a grind.
trophies.name: On the Spot
